planting.note: Plant container-grown vines after frost danger passes on a sturdy overhead trellis or pergola, siting a male Actinidia chinensis pollenizer within about 30 feet since the vine is dioecious.

directions: Bred in Sichuan, China, Hongyang is prized for the ring of red pigment surrounding the core of its otherwise pale-gold flesh, with an especially sweet, low-acid flavor compared with standard green kiwi. Grow it on a permanent overhead arbor in full sun and rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, pairing it with a male vine for pollination. This cultivar became notorious in the early 2010s for extreme susceptibility to bacterial canker (Psa), which devastated red-fleshed kiwifruit orchards across China, so prioritize open canopy pruning, avoid overhead irrigation, and sanitize tools between vines. Harvest when fruit firms and sugar content rises, then finish ripening at room temperature.
sources: Sichuan Academy of Natural Resource Sciences — kiwifruit cultivar records
New Zealand Institute for Plant and Food Research — Psa bacterial canker studies

planting.note: Train young vines onto a heavy-gauge T-bar or overhead trellis right after the last frost, and plant a male Actinidia chinensis vine nearby for pollination.

directions: Developed by the Wuhan Botanical Garden of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Jin Yan bears smooth, nearly hairless gold-fleshed fruit noted for unusually high vitamin C content and a mild sweet-tart flavor, ripening earlier than most green-fleshed kiwi. Site it in full sun on fertile, well-drained ground and give the vigorous vine a strong permanent trellis from planting day. Because gold-fleshed Actinidia chinensis selections are more vulnerable to bacterial canker (Psa) than green kiwi, keep the canopy open through annual pruning and keep irrigation off the foliage. Pick fruit firm and ripen it at room temperature for best eating quality.
sources: Wuhan Botanical Garden, Chinese Academy of Sciences — kiwifruit breeding program
China Fruit Tree Records — Actinidia cultivar registry

planting.note: Give vines wind shelter and a permanent overhead trellis, and plant a compatible male Actinidia chinensis vine nearby since the species is dioecious.

directions: Bred in Sichuan, China as a smooth-skinned, cylindrical gold-fleshed kiwifruit, Jintao has sweet, lower-acid flavor and was grown both for the domestic Chinese market and limited export. Plant it on a permanent overhead trellis in full sun with rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, and mulch the root zone heavily in regions near the cooler edge of its hardiness range. Watch closely for bacterial canker (Psa), which spreads readily among gold-fleshed Actinidia chinensis cultivars in wet or poorly ventilated plantings, and remove any cankered wood promptly. Harvest firm and ripen off the vine for best flavor.
sources: Sichuan Academy of Natural Resource Sciences — kiwifruit cultivar records
New Zealand Plant Variety Rights Office — Actinidia cultivar records

planting.note: Plant after frost danger passes onto a sturdy pergola or overhead trellis in a sheltered, full-sun spot, pairing with a male Actinidia chinensis vine for pollination.

directions: Bred by France's INRA fruit research program, Soreli is a gold-fleshed kiwifruit selection suited to mild European-style growing regions, producing smooth, low-fuzz skin and sweet, aromatic yellow flesh that ripens notably earlier than standard green 'Hayward' kiwi. Grow it on a sturdy overhead trellis or pergola in full sun and deep, well-drained soil, with a compatible male Actinidia chinensis vine planted nearby for fruit set. Its comparatively modest winter chilling requirement makes it workable in borderline mild-winter areas, though late spring frost can still damage emerging shoots. As with other gold-fleshed kiwifruit, favor good airflow and avoid wetting foliage to limit bacterial canker (Psa) pressure.
sources: INRA (French National Institute for Agricultural Research) — Actinidia breeding program
Ctifl (Centre Technique Interprofessionnel des Fruits et Légumes) — kiwifruit variety notes
